newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-COLUMBUS CREW CLINCHES MLS PLAYOFF SPOT AS SEASON ENDS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COLUMBUS CREW CLINCHES MLS PLAYOFF SPOT AS SEASON ENDS.

text.p: The Columbus Crew, longshots to reach the Major League Soccer playoffs a month ago, completed a miracle turnaround by claiming a post-season berth with a 1-0 win over the New England Revolution.

Brian McBride scored in the 37th minute Saturday and U.S. international goalkeeper Brad Friedel recorded his fourth shutout for the Crew, which won for the ninth time in 10 games for coach Tom Fitzgerald.
Fitzgerald replaced Timo Liekoski on August 2, when the Crew (15-17) was 6-16 and mired in last place in the Eastern Conference.
The Crew host first-place Tampa Bay Mutiny in the best-of-three conference semifinals on Wednesday, with the second game in Tampa on Saturday.

The Mutiny (20-12) completed the season with two victories. They outlasted the San Jose Clash in a shootout in San Jose on Thursday and then rolled to a 4-1 win over the New York/New Jersey MetroStars in Tampa on Saturday.
Striker Roy Lassister scored twice in Saturday's win to finish the inaugural MLS season as league's leading scorer with 27 goals.

Venezuelan native Giovanni Savarese converted a penalty kick for the MetroStars (15-17), who clinched a playoff berth and third place with a 1-0 triumph over Columbus on a goal by Colombian Antony De Avila on Wednesday.
New York will face D.C. United in the first round of the playoffs.
United (16-16) tuned up for post-season play with a pair of victories, stopping New England (15-17) 3-2 on an 89th-minute goal by El Salvadoran Raul Diaz Arce on Tuesday.
Arce added two more tallies in United's 3-1 home win over the Colorado Rapids (11-21) Saturday, to finish with 23 goals.

The Los Angeles Galaxy (19-13), which won only seven of its last 20 games after getting off to a fast start, clinched first place in the Western Conference with a pair of 2-1 victories over the Dallas Burn (17-15).
On Thursday, Greg Vanney broke a 1-1 tie in the second half. On Sunday, Arash Noamouz and John Garvey scored in the final 14 minutes before Ted Eck tallied for Dallas in the 89th.
The Galaxy will open their post-season against fourth-place San Jose (15-17).
San Jose closed out its season with a 1-0 shootout win over the Wiz (17-15) in Kansas City on Saturday as Paul Bravo converted the game-winning attempt in the tie-breaker.
Kansas City will take on Dallas in the other conference semifinal series.
